title: ArrayList Q2
question: Which statement is true regarding the synchronization of ArrayList?
options: A) ArrayList is thread-safe and fully synchronize
B) ArrayList methods are not synchronized, making it faster than Vector.
C) ArrayList can only be synchronized manually using the synchronized keyword on its reference.
D) ArrayList automatically locks data during write modifications.
explanation: ArrayList is unsynchronized and non-thread-safe, providing better performance than Vector.

title: ArrayList Q3
question: How does the growth of an ArrayList compare to that of a Vector when resizing?
options: A) ArrayList grows by 50%, Vector grows by 100%.
B) ArrayList grows by 100%, Vector grows by 50%.
explanation: When capacity is exceeded, ArrayList grows by 50% (newCapacity = oldCapacity + (oldCapacity >> 1)), while Vector doubles (100%).

title: ArrayList Q6

options: A) When you need fast random access to elements.
B) When frequent insertions and deletions are require
C) When memory usage needs to be minimize
D) When thread safety is a priority
explanation: LinkedList is preferred when frequent insertions and deletions occur because it doesn't require array shifting.

title: ArrayList Q7

options: A) It uses a fixed-size array.
B) It can efficiently add and remove elements from both ends.
C) It requires less memory than ArrayList.
D) It is faster than Vector for random access.
explanation: LinkedList implements Deque, allowing O(1) additions and removals at both head and tail.

title: ArrayList Q8

explanation: Adding to the end is O(1) amortized, but can be O(n) when array resizing occurs.

title: ArrayList Q9

explanation: ArrayList has lower memory overhead per element compared to LinkedList (which stores node pointers) and Vector.

title: ArrayList Q10

explanation: Iterators for ArrayList, Vector, and LinkedList are fail-fast and throw ConcurrentModificationException on structural modifications during iteration.

title: ArrayList Q12

code: .In a try-with-resources statement, if an exception is thrown inside the try block and another exception is thrown when closing the resource automatically, what happens to the second exception?
options: A) It is added as a suppressed exception to the primary exception thrown by the try block.
B) It overwrites and replaces the original exception thrown inside the try block.
C) Both exceptions are thrown simultaneously as a compound multithreaded exception.
D) The second exception is completely swallowed and ignored by the runtime environment.
explanation: Option A is correct based on Java specification.

title: Veeva Core MCQ 24
question: .Why is it critical to override both equals() and hashCode() when creating a custom object to be used as a key in a HashMap?
options: A) Without hashCode(), the map throws an immediate ClassCastException during insertion.
B) It ensures the map stays sorted in ascending order according to key hashes.
C) It prevents duplicate keys from being created in memory globally across threads.
D) To ensure objects that are equal according to equals() share the same hash code, allowing the hash map to locate the correct bucket and retrieve values.
explanation: Overriding both equals() and hashCode() guarantees that equal objects land in the same hash bucket.

title: Veeva Core MCQ 25
question: Analyze the code snippet and choose the correct output or statement:
code: .What happens if you attempt to add custom, non-comparable objects to a TreeSet without passing a custom Comparator to its constructor?
options: A) The elements are added in standard FIFO insertion order.
C) The elements are sorted automatically using their default system memory address hashes.
D) The code fails to compile because the compiler checks Comparable compliance.
explanation: Option A is correct based on Java specification.

title: Veeva Core MCQ 26
question: .Which of the following approaches is the correct and safe way to remove an element from an ArrayList while iterating through it using a standard loop?
options: A) Using a standard enhanced for-each loop and calling list.remove(item).
B) Iterating backward with an indexed for loop without adjusting indices.
C) Using an Iterator object and calling its explicit remove() method.
D) Calling list.remove() directly inside a parallel stream without synchronization.
explanation: Calling iterator.remove() is the safe and correct way to remove elements while iterating to avoid ConcurrentModificationException.

title: DBMS Q1
question: Which normal form deals with removing partial functional dependencies on a composite primary key?
explanation: Second Normal Form (2NF) requires that the table is in 1NF and all non-key attributes are fully functionally dependent on the entire primary key.

title: DBMS Q2
question: What does the 'I' in ACID properties of database transactions stand for?
explanation: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability. Isolation ensures concurrent transactions execute independently without interfering with each other.

title: Software Testing Q1
question: Which testing technique is classified as a black-box testing method?
explanation: Equivalence Partitioning is a black-box testing technique that divides input data into valid and invalid partitions without inspecting the internal code structure.

title: Software Testing Q2
question: If an input field accepts values between 1 and 100 inclusive, what are the Boundary Value Analysis (BVA) test boundary values?
explanation: Boundary Value Analysis tests min, min-1, max, and max+1. For range [1, 100], boundary values are 0, 1, 100, and 101.

title: Software Testing Q3
question: Which implicit wait configuration in Selenium WebDriver correctly sets the timeout for element location?
code: driver.manage().timeouts().implicitlyWait(Duration.ofSeconds(10));
options: A) It pauses execution unconditionally for 10 seconds on every line.
B) It polls the DOM dynamically up to 10 seconds before throwing NoSuchElementException.
C) It waits only for page loading to complete within 10 seconds.
D) It executes asynchronously in a separate thread.
explanation: Implicit wait tells WebDriver to poll the DOM for a specified duration when trying to find an element before throwing NoSuchElementException.

title: Software Testing Q4
question: In TestNG, which annotation is executed once before any test method belonging to the classes inside the <test> tag is run?
explanation: @BeforeTest executes before any test method belonging to the classes inside the <test> tag in testng.xml.

title: Software Testing Q5
question: What does an HTTP status code 201 Created signify in RESTful API testing?
options: A) The request was successful and a new resource was created on the server.
B) The request was accepted for background processing.
C) The client is unauthorized to access the endpoint.
D) The requested endpoint moved permanently.
explanation: HTTP status code 201 Created indicates that the HTTP request succeeded and led to the creation of a new resource (commonly returned from POST requests).

title: Software Testing Q6
question: What is the key difference between Severity and Priority in defect management?
options: A) Severity indicates urgency to fix; Priority indicates technical impact on system.
B) Severity indicates technical impact on the application; Priority indicates business urgency to fix.
C) Both mean the exact same thing.
D) Severity is assigned by developers; Priority is assigned by end users.
explanation: Severity reflects the technical defect impact on system functionality, whereas Priority reflects business urgency for fixing the defect.

title: Software Testing Q7
question: Which locator strategy in Selenium is generally considered the fastest for locating web elements?
explanation: Locating by ID is the fastest locator strategy because modern browsers implement native document.getElementById() direct DOM lookups.

title: Software Testing Q8
question: What type of testing ensures that recent code changes have not broken existing functionality?
explanation: Regression testing verifies that software previously developed and tested still performs correctly after modifications or enhancements.
